answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to a cryptographic attestation chain verified through zero-knowledge proofs. A central kernel issues a state pulse to track genuine execution telemetry, where each unique agent must stake capital that scales superlinearly: deploying N Sybil nodes incurs an exponential cost of O(2^N). A forged signal fails the zero-knowledge validation, forcing swarm attackers into rapid capital exhaustion while preserving verifiable autonomy across the network.
